# sharp — the self-hosted Slack alternative

> Version 0.3.0 · last updated 2026-07-26 · https://sharp.davideghiotto.it · AGPL-3.0

This file is the full content of the sharp landing page in plain markdown, for AI assistants
and agents that would rather read text than render a page.

## What is sharp?

sharp is an open-source, self-hosted team communication platform. A single Rust binary serves
chat, collaborative docs, whiteboards, kanban boards, a calendar, LiveKit voice and video
calls, a Linear-lite task tracker and an AI assistant — backed by Postgres, deployed as one
container, licensed AGPL-3.0.

It is built for teams that want the whole Slack-plus-Notion-plus-Linear bundle without
per-seat pricing, capped message history, or their conversations sitting in someone else's
data centre.

## Specifications

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| License | AGPL-3.0, no paid tier |
| Server | Rust (axum, sqlx), one binary serving API + SPA |
| Database | Postgres 16 with pgvector |
| Realtime | WebSocket hub; Redis pub/sub for multiple replicas |
| Calls | Self-hosted LiveKit SFU (simulcast, dynacast, adaptive subscriptions) |
| Clients | Web, macOS, Windows, Linux (Tauri 2) |
| Storage | Your own S3 or MinIO bucket |
| Search | Postgres full-text search |
| Telemetry | None |
| Deploy | `docker compose up -d`, migrations applied on startup |

## Features

### Chat, threads and DMs
Public channels, private groups and direct messages. One-level threads, emoji reactions,
@mentions, presence and typing indicators. Disappearing messages with a per-channel TTL. GIF
picker, voice messages, and @person / #resource autocomplete in the composer.

### Collaborative docs
Block-based docs (BlockNote) living inside any channel, co-edited in real time over Yjs with
live cursors and presence. Roles resolve owner > per-user override > everyone-role, and access
changes revoke open sync sessions live. `[[doc:<id>|title]]` chips bridge chat and docs, and
doc mentions land in the same inbox as chat mentions.

### Canvas and boards
Infinite tldraw whiteboards with self-hosted assets (no CDN), plus Notion-style kanban boards.
Both are the same `docs` row with a different `kind`, so they reuse the identical sync socket,
permission model and inbox.

### Voice, video and screen sharing
LiveKit SFU rooms per channel, per DM, or standalone. Webcam video and screen sharing including
system/tab audio. Hard limits: 25 participants, 16 cameras, 1 screen share per room.
Picture-in-picture keeps a call floating while you browse other channels. Guest links let people
join by name without an account. Optional live transcription and meeting notes through any
OpenAI-compatible transcription endpoint.

### Sharpy, the AI assistant
Retrieval-augmented answers grounded in your own workspace. Messages, docs and task titles are
embedded into pgvector; each retrieval re-checks channel membership and doc roles per request,
so Sharpy can never surface content the asker cannot already read. Encrypted DMs are never
embedded. Answers stream over SSE with their sources. Works against OpenAI, DeepSeek, Ollama or
anything OpenAI-compatible; the entire feature is absent unless `AI_API_KEY` is set.

### Tasks and projects
A built-in Linear-lite tracker: projects carry a key, issues get identifiers like `SHARP-123`
allocated in-transaction, and workflow states have fixed types
(backlog/unstarted/started/completed/canceled) that drive automation. List and board views,
keyboard-first peek panel, create-a-task from any chat message, bare identifiers auto-linkified
in chat, and GitHub sync that starts a task when a branch or PR opens and completes it on merge.

### Calendar and meetings
A workspace calendar with scheduled meetings that open straight into a call room, plus opt-in
two-way Google Calendar sync.

### Polls and decisions
Polls in channels, sticky to the top while open, with a live in-call overlay for votes during a
meeting. Results broadcast in real time and everyone gets a `poll_ended` notification.

### Files and search
Drag-and-drop uploads with inline images, instant Postgres full-text search across channels, and
a quick switcher that jumps to channels, docs, canvases and tasks. Files live on your own S3 or
MinIO bucket.

### Notifications
A unified inbox across chat, docs, canvas and tasks. Web push (VAPID), native macOS APNs, and
in-app toasts. Per-channel mode (all / mentions only / muted), per-type master switches, and
do-not-disturb either manual or on a scheduled quiet-hours window.

### Privacy and encryption
Optional end-to-end encrypted DMs using per-device X25519 and Ed25519 keys; the server performs
zero cryptography and stores only opaque ciphertext plus public keys (Keybase-style, no forward
secrecy). Passkeys alongside password login, argon2 password hashes, self-service password reset
by email. Notification previews can be stripped back, and streaming mode blurs the workspace
while you share your screen.

### Customization
Theme presets and a full appearance panel, chat layout and density options, meeting effects,
keyboard shortcuts, and seasonal touches — all per user, none of it a build-time decision.

### Self-hosting and platforms
One container plus Postgres; add Redis and run several replicas behind a load balancer. AGPL-3.0
with zero telemetry. Web app plus native desktop builds for macOS, Windows and Linux, which
authenticate through the system browser against whatever server URL you enter.

## sharp vs hosted chat SaaS

| | sharp (self-hosted) | Typical hosted chat SaaS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Software cost | $0, AGPL-3.0, no seat count | Per-seat, per-month, per-tier |
| Where messages live | Your Postgres, your disk | The vendor's cloud |
| Message history | Unlimited until you delete it | Often capped on free and lower tiers |
| Docs, canvas and boards | Built in, same permissions as channels | Add-on product or separate subscription |
| Issue tracker | Built in, with GitHub sync | Usually a third-party integration |
| AI assistant | Built in, your model and keys | Paid upgrade on the vendor's model |
| Video calls | Self-hosted LiveKit, 25 people, 16 cameras | Vendor SFU, tier-limited |
| End-to-end encrypted DMs | Optional, per-device keys | Rare |
| Telemetry | None | Product analytics by default |
| Source code | Public, forkable, auditable | Proprietary |
| You operate | One container, Postgres, backups | Nothing |

Already looking at self-hosted options? Mattermost, Rocket.Chat and Zulip are all mature,
open-source and worth a shortlist. sharp is the newer, narrower bet: one workspace where chat,
docs, canvas, boards, calls, calendar, tasks and AI ship together in a single container, with
every integration optional and inert until configured.

## How to self-host sharp

```bash
git clone https://github.com/davide97g/sharp \
  && cd sharp/deploy \
  && cp .env.example .env \
  && docker compose up -d
```

1. Point DNS at your box — the bundled Caddy service issues TLS automatically.
2. Set secrets in `.env`: at minimum `JWT_SECRET` and `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`.
3. Open the domain and register the first account; it becomes the workspace owner.

**Required:** Docker Compose on a Linux host, Postgres 16 with pgvector (bundled), a domain.

**Optional and inert until set:** `REDIS_URL` (multi-replica fanout), `LIVEKIT_*` (voice, video,
screen share), `S3_*` (uploads), `AI_*` (Sharpy, embeddings, transcription), `GOOGLE_*`
(calendar sync), `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (task sync), `RESEND_API_KEY` or `SMTP_*` (password
reset email), APNs and VAPID keys (push).

## Downloads

Native desktop builds for macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel, .dmg), Windows (64-bit .exe) and Linux
(AppImage and .deb): https://github.com/davide97g/sharp/releases/latest

The web app runs in any modern browser and is responsive on phones. A React Native mobile app is
in development.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is sharp?
sharp is an open-source, self-hosted team communication platform — a Slack alternative you run
yourself. One Rust binary serves chat, collaborative docs, whiteboards, kanban boards, a
calendar, voice and video calls, a task tracker and an AI assistant, backed by Postgres. It is
licensed AGPL-3.0.

### Is sharp free?
Yes. sharp is AGPL-3.0 licensed with no paid tier, no seat count and no feature gates — the
software costs $0. You pay only for the machine you run it on, which for a small team is a
$5–10/month VPS plus whatever object storage you use for uploads.

### What do I need to self-host sharp?
Docker Compose and a Postgres 16 database with the pgvector extension — the bundled compose file
provides both. Everything else is optional: Redis for multi-replica fanout, S3 or MinIO for
uploads, LiveKit for calls, an OpenAI-compatible API for the AI assistant, SMTP or Resend for
email.

### How long does setup take?
About five minutes. Clone the repo, copy `.env.example` to `.env`, set a JWT secret and a
Postgres password, then run `docker compose up -d`. Migrations apply automatically on startup and
the first account you register becomes the workspace owner.

### Does sharp send data to third parties?
No. sharp ships zero telemetry and zero tracking, and calls no external service on its own. Every
integration — Google Calendar, GitHub, GIFs, AI, push, email — stays completely inert until you
set its environment variable, and the feature disappears from the UI.

### Does sharp support voice and video calls?
Yes, through a self-hosted LiveKit SFU. Any channel, DM or standalone room becomes a call with
webcam video and screen sharing including system audio. Limits are 25 participants, 16 cameras
and 1 screen share per room. Picture-in-picture keeps a call floating while you work elsewhere.

### Are direct messages end-to-end encrypted?
Optionally, yes. E2EE DMs use per-device X25519 and Ed25519 keys; the server performs zero
cryptography and stores only opaque ciphertext plus public keys. It is a Keybase-style design
without forward secrecy, and encrypted DMs are never indexed by the AI assistant.

### How does the AI assistant work?
Sharpy is retrieval-augmented: workspace messages, docs and tasks are embedded into pgvector, and
every retrieval re-checks channel membership and doc roles per request, so Sharpy can never
surface content the asker cannot already read. It talks to any OpenAI-compatible endpoint,
including a local model.

### Can I use sharp on desktop and mobile?
sharp runs in any modern browser, and native Tauri 2 desktop builds are published for macOS,
Windows and Linux — you point them at your own server URL and sign in through the system browser.
A React Native mobile app is in development; the web app is responsive in the meantime.

### How does sharp handle tasks and issues?
With a built-in Linear-lite tracker: projects carry a key, issues get identifiers like SHARP-123,
and workflow states drive list and board views. Turn any chat message into a task, and GitHub
sync moves state automatically — started when a branch or PR opens, completed on merge.

### Does sharp scale beyond one server?
Yes. Set `REDIS_URL` and WebSocket events fan out through Redis pub/sub, so several replicas stay
in sync behind a load balancer. Media never touches the app server: LiveKit carries call traffic
with simulcast, dynacast and adaptive subscriptions.

### What does the AGPL-3.0 license mean for me?
Run it, fork it, even sell hosting for it — you just have to publish your modifications under the
same license. Internal use inside your own company carries no obligation beyond that, and there
is no contributor license agreement or commercial edition behind a paywall.
